# Project Development Guide

This guide documents the CLI commands used to maintain the Modular Monolith structure of the LibraryApp solution.

## 1. Adding a New Module

Replace `{ModuleName}` with the name of your new module (e.g., `Borrowing`, `Notifications`).

### Step 1: Create Project Libraries
Run these commands from the solution root directory:
```bash
dotnet new classlib -o src/Modules/{ModuleName}/LibraryApp.{ModuleName}.Domain
dotnet new classlib -o src/Modules/{ModuleName}/LibraryApp.{ModuleName}.Application
dotnet new classlib -o src/Modules/{ModuleName}/LibraryApp.{ModuleName}.Infrastructure
dotnet new classlib -o src/Modules/{ModuleName}/LibraryApp.{ModuleName}.Contracts
```

### Step 2: Setup Project Dependencies
Link the standard dependencies between internal layers and shared libraries:

```bash
# Application references Domain and Shared.Contracts
dotnet add src/Modules/{ModuleName}/LibraryApp.{ModuleName}.Application/LibraryApp.{ModuleName}.Application.csproj reference src/Modules/{ModuleName}/LibraryApp.{ModuleName}.Domain/LibraryApp.{ModuleName}.Domain.csproj
dotnet add src/Modules/{ModuleName}/LibraryApp.{ModuleName}.Application/LibraryApp.{ModuleName}.Application.csproj reference src/Shared/LibraryApp.Shared.Contracts/LibraryApp.Shared.Contracts.csproj

# Infrastructure references Application and Contracts
dotnet add src/Modules/{ModuleName}/LibraryApp.{ModuleName}.Infrastructure/LibraryApp.{ModuleName}.Infrastructure.csproj reference src/Modules/{ModuleName}/LibraryApp.{ModuleName}.Application/LibraryApp.{ModuleName}.Application.csproj
dotnet add src/Modules/{ModuleName}/LibraryApp.{ModuleName}.Infrastructure/LibraryApp.{ModuleName}.Infrastructure.csproj reference src/Modules/{ModuleName}/LibraryApp.{ModuleName}.Contracts/LibraryApp.{ModuleName}.Contracts.csproj

# Domain references Shared
dotnet add src/Modules/{ModuleName}/LibraryApp.{ModuleName}.Domain/LibraryApp.{ModuleName}.Domain.csproj reference src/Shared/LibraryApp.Shared.Contracts/LibraryApp.Shared.Contracts.csproj
dotnet add src/Modules/{ModuleName}/LibraryApp.{ModuleName}.Domain/LibraryApp.{ModuleName}.Domain.csproj reference src/Shared/LibraryApp.Shared.Domain/LibraryApp.Shared.Domain.csproj

# Contracts reference Shared
dotnet add src/Modules/{ModuleName}/LibraryApp.{ModuleName}.Contracts/LibraryApp.{ModuleName}.Contracts.csproj reference src/Shared/LibraryApp.Shared.Contracts/LibraryApp.Shared.Contracts.csproj
```

### Step 3: Install Common NuGet Packages
Install core packages required by most infrastructure and application layers:

```bash
# Install MediatR in Application
dotnet add src/Modules/{ModuleName}/LibraryApp.{ModuleName}.Application/LibraryApp.{ModuleName}.Application.csproj package MediatR

# Install MediatR and EF Core packages in Infrastructure
dotnet add src/Modules/{ModuleName}/LibraryApp.{ModuleName}.Infrastructure/LibraryApp.{ModuleName}.Infrastructure.csproj package MediatR
dotnet add src/Modules/{ModuleName}/LibraryApp.{ModuleName}.Infrastructure/LibraryApp.{ModuleName}.Infrastructure.csproj package Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.SqlServer
dotnet add src/Modules/{ModuleName}/LibraryApp.{ModuleName}.Infrastructure/LibraryApp.{ModuleName}.Infrastructure.csproj package Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Tools
```

### Step 4: Link Module to API
Reference your module's interface and implementation inside the API startup project:
```bash
dotnet add src/API/LibraryApp.API/LibraryApp.API.csproj reference src/Modules/{ModuleName}/LibraryApp.{ModuleName}.Infrastructure/LibraryApp.{ModuleName}.Infrastructure.csproj
dotnet add src/API/LibraryApp.API/LibraryApp.API.csproj reference src/Modules/{ModuleName}/LibraryApp.{ModuleName}.Contracts/LibraryApp.{ModuleName}.Contracts.csproj
```

---

## 2. Registering Projects to the Solution
To include the newly created module projects in the main solution tree:
```bash
dotnet sln LibraryApp.sln add src/Modules/{ModuleName}/LibraryApp.{ModuleName}.Domain/LibraryApp.{ModuleName}.Domain.csproj
dotnet sln LibraryApp.sln add src/Modules/{ModuleName}/LibraryApp.{ModuleName}.Application/LibraryApp.{ModuleName}.Application.csproj
dotnet sln LibraryApp.sln add src/Modules/{ModuleName}/LibraryApp.{ModuleName}.Infrastructure/LibraryApp.{ModuleName}.Infrastructure.csproj
dotnet sln LibraryApp.sln add src/Modules/{ModuleName}/LibraryApp.{ModuleName}.Contracts/LibraryApp.{ModuleName}.Contracts.csproj
```

---

## 3. Database Migrations (EF Core CLI)

Since each module owns its boundary and typically has its own `DbContext` (e.g., `CatalogDbContext`, `MemberDbContext`), you MUST specify the specific context and project paths when managing migrations.

### Add a New Migration
```bash
dotnet ef migrations add {MigrationName} \
  --project src/Modules/{ModuleName}/LibraryApp.{ModuleName}.Infrastructure/LibraryApp.{ModuleName}.Infrastructure.csproj \
  --startup-project src/API/LibraryApp.API/LibraryApp.API.csproj \
  --context {ModuleName}DbContext
```
*Example for adding "InitialSchema" to Catalog:*
```bash
dotnet ef migrations add InitialSchema --project src/Modules/Catalog/LibraryApp.Catalog.Infrastructure/LibraryApp.Catalog.Infrastructure.csproj --startup-project src/API/LibraryApp.API/LibraryApp.API.csproj --context CatalogDbContext
```

### Update the Database
Applies all pending migrations to the database.
```bash
dotnet ef database update \
  --project src/Modules/{ModuleName}/LibraryApp.{ModuleName}.Infrastructure/LibraryApp.{ModuleName}.Infrastructure.csproj \
  --startup-project src/API/LibraryApp.API/LibraryApp.API.csproj \
  --context {ModuleName}DbContext
```
*Example for updating Catalog db:*
```bash
dotnet ef database update --project src/Modules/Catalog/LibraryApp.Catalog.Infrastructure/LibraryApp.Catalog.Infrastructure.csproj --startup-project src/API/LibraryApp.API/LibraryApp.API.csproj --context CatalogDbContext
```

### Remove Last Migration
Reverts the last local migration that hasn't been applied/committed yet.
```bash
dotnet ef migrations remove \
  --project src/Modules/{ModuleName}/LibraryApp.{ModuleName}.Infrastructure/LibraryApp.{ModuleName}.Infrastructure.csproj \
  --startup-project src/API/LibraryApp.API/LibraryApp.API.csproj \
  --context {ModuleName}DbContext
```
